problem: Existing language-driven zero-shot navigation methods (SG-Nav, InstructNav) explore without priori maps and target object categories, so they fail in functional buildings (schools, hospitals) where rooms look alike and are distinguishable only by landmarks; VLMs also reason poorly over raw map images.
motivation: Functional buildings have standardized but complex, open layouts with highly similar features, and service robots need to work there, yet almost no research or simulation environments exist. Humans navigate them by combining a priori map and landmarks, which motivates mimicking this behavior.
key_idea: Convert the environment map into a segment-based semantic priori-map, have a VLM plan a global path with a hierarchical CoT prompt plus an annotated map, and execute it landmark by landmark using VLM coarse actions refined by GroundingDINO+SAM+PixelNav.
insight: Structuring the map as text-like room/path segments and using H-CoT prompts is what makes VLM planning work: ordinary prompt with raw map gets 31.3/10.4/0.0 planning SR (easy/medium/hard), while H-CoT with map gets 91.6/85.4/75.0 and annotated priori-map 95.8/89.5/83.3. The fine-grained refinement is also essential: coarse VLM actions alone give 32/10/0 SR versus 88/68/46 with refinement. Localization degrades sharply when landmarks are scarce (SR 63.3, SDF 25.0).
method: Map Parsing: a Tkinter tool annotates room IDs and key path waypoints (start, turn, branch, end fork); the path is split into segments linked to the nearest rooms, e.g. seg13(room14-room7), giving a structured semantic priori-map (done once per environment).

VLM Planning (H-CoT): a three-step hierarchical chain-of-thought prompt (relative position of agent and target, key waypoints, first-person actions), combined with an annotated priori-map image and directional relations between segments, outputs a global plan that is decomposed into landmark-to-landmark sub-goals.
Localization: the agent captures images at 30/90/150/210/270/330 degrees and needs to identify any two landmarks to determine its position; otherwise it keeps exploring along the path.

Coarse action generation: the robot captures six views stitched into a panorama with angle annotations; the VLM finds the target landmark and predicts a coarse direction (about 30-degree granularity). Views at 0, ±30, ±60, ±90 degrees are searched during navigation, excluding the one implied by the previous action.
Fine action refinement: GroundingDINO + SAM mask the landmark, and the mask center plus the first-person view go into a fine-tuned PixelNav network that outputs a precise direction.

Action prediction at unobservable places: outputs current and next action together (e.g. room8: go straight -> turn2: turn left); corners are distinguished from corridors by the wall/floor mask ratio in front of the robot.
Closed loop: target determination -> search -> verification -> target update, advancing to the next landmark once the current one is detected.

setting.backbone: Unspecified VLM for planning and coarse actions (frozen) + GroundingDINO + SAM + fine-tuned PixelNav network
setting.training_data: VLM, GroundingDINO and SAM are used as-is; PixelNav is fine-tuned on unspecified data; the FB simulation environments are built from VA Design Guide maps
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB panoramas stitched from multi-direction views (camera at 1.6 m, 60 degree HFOV), plus a priori environment map
setting.action_space: Coarse direction / turn commands (about 30 degree steps) refined to fine angles; go straight, turn left/right, fork selection
setting.simulator: Gazebo (6 self-built functional-building scenes) + real world
setting.privileged: A priori environment map of the building (parsed and annotated by hand) and landmark information

numbers_note: Only the paper's own home-made FB benchmark (simulation and real) is evaluated; no standard benchmarks. Number of episodes and the specific VLM are not stated.
results: On the home-made FB simulation set, PM-Nav reaches SR 88/68/46 (easy/medium/hard) versus SG-Nav 12/4/0 and InstructNav 18/8/0. In the real school it gets SR 75/55/15 versus 10/0/0 (SG-Nav) and 15/0/0 (InstructNav).
limitations: Environment map parsing is manual/semi-manual, and end-to-end map parsing accuracy remains unsolved
Low exploration efficiency with unnecessary traversal; localization degrades when landmarks are scarce (SR 63.3)

Evaluated only on a self-built dataset with SG-Nav/InstructNav baselines that are not designed for room-level landmark navigation; the VLM and episode counts are unspecified, and real hard-task SR is only 15%
